content: 1. Rehabilitation is a collection of interventions aimed at optimizing an individual’s functional abilities and minimizing disability in the context of their health condition and environment. 2. Health conditions encompass a wide range of issues, including acute or chronic diseases, disorders, injuries, or trauma. They may also include other circumstances such as pregnancy, aging, stress, congenital anomalies, or genetic predispositions. 3. Rehabilitation enables individuals to maximize their potential to live, work, and learn effectively. 4. Evidence indicates that rehabilitation can alleviate functional difficulties associated with aging and enhance overall quality of life. 5. Recommendations for rehabilitation services are a response to the World Report on Disability, which urges Member States to develop, implement, and monitor policies, regulatory mechanisms, and standards for rehabilitation services while promoting access to these services. 6. These recommendations also align with Objective 2 of the WHO Global Disability Action Plan 2014–2021, which focuses on strengthening and expanding rehabilitation, habilitation, assistive technology, and community-based rehabilitation services. 7. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities calls on Member States to take appropriate measures to organize, strengthen, and expand rehabilitation services and programs. 8. Currently, there is limited information available to guide countries in strengthening rehabilitation within health systems to meet the growing demand for these services. 9. The recommendations aim to address this information gap by providing system-level guidance for improving the delivery of rehabilitation services. 10. The objective of these recommendations is to offer evidence-based, expert-informed guidance to assist governments and stakeholders in developing and expanding equitable rehabilitation services across all levels of health systems and service delivery platforms. 11. The recommendations advocate for a multidisciplinary workforce and sustainable funding mechanisms to support and maintain high-quality rehabilitation service delivery. 12. These recommendations are intended for government leaders, health policymakers, and stakeholders involved in workforce development, training, financing, research, and assistive products. 13. The recommendations focus exclusively on rehabilitation within the context of health systems, addressing service delivery and financing while leaving leadership, governance, workforce, and information systems for future WHO publications. 14. The overarching principles emphasize that rehabilitation is an integral component of comprehensive, person-centered care, ensuring individuals can achieve their full functional potential in their living and working environments. 15. Rehabilitation services are relevant across the continuum of care, from preventing impairments in the acute phase to optimizing and maintaining functioning in post-acute and long-term phases. 16. Rehabilitation is a critical part of universal health coverage, requiring efforts to improve the quality, accessibility, and affordability of services. 17. Policies and interventions must address the diverse needs for rehabilitation services across different population groups and geographic areas to ensure equitable access to high-quality services. 18. The recommendations are based on rigorous evidence collection, review, and assessment, ensuring transparency and systematic decision-making. 19. The strength of each recommendation is determined by weighing the balance of benefits versus harms, stakeholder values, resource implications, and evidence quality. 20. Rehabilitation services should be integrated into health systems rather than social or welfare systems to improve coordination with medical and health services, accountability, quality assurance, and sustainability. 21. The integration of rehabilitation into health systems is essential to meet the anticipated increase in demand for these services and to address the challenges associated with fragmented governance. 22. The recommendations aim to ensure that effective, safe, and high-quality rehabilitation interventions are accessible to those in need, minimizing resource waste and strengthening health systems.
